headline: Approved certificates of appropriateness for 73 Main Street and 139 Main Street projects.
summary: The commission adopted findings and decisions for 30 Central Street and approved a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior changes at 73 Main Street, including a condition about removing a square box panel. It also approved a Certificate of Appropriateness for window and door replacements at 139 Main Street.
decisions: Adopted the findings and decisions for 30 Central Street.

Granted a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review Permit for 73 Main Street, with the condition that the square box panel above the second window be removed if possible, or painted to match if not.
Granted a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review for 139 Main Street.

Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
August 13th, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING OF AUGUST 13, 2026, 7:00 P.M. 
 COUNCIL CHAMBERS, CITY HALL 
73 HARLOW STREET  
 
 
MEETING MINUTES  
 
Commission Members Present:   Nathaniel King 
       Katie Coe 
       Matthew Weitkamp 
       Peter Keebler 
Rebecca Krupke 
Peter Sachs    
  
             
City Staff Present: Anja Collette, Planning Officer  
Matt Altiero, Planning Analyst 
Mike Pullen, HPC Consultant 
 
Chair King called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M. 
______________________________________________________________________ 
 
Old Business: 
1. Meeting Minutes –  July 9, 2026  
 
Commissioner Sachs moved to approve the July 9th meeting minutes. Seconded by Commissioner 
Krupke. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
2. Adoption of Findings & Decision for 30 Central Street 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved to adopt the findings and decisions for 30 Central Street. Seconded by 
Commissioner Krupke. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
New Business: 
 
3. Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review – 73 Main Street – Map-Lot 041-
066 – Main Street Historic District – Applicant: Roscoe Witham - Owner: Cook
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
August 13th, 2026 
Investment Group LLC - The applicant, Roscoe Witham, requests approval for 
Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review at property located at 73 Main Street 
for the replacement of siding panels with brick veneer and replacement of tiles on the 
underside of the awning with in-kind materials. Additionally, the applicant proposes an 
installation of two walk-up sliding service windows facing Cross Street. The property is 
located at Map-Lot 042-106 in the Main Street Historic District. Applicant: Roscoe 
Witham. Owner: Cook Investment Group LLC. 
 
Chair King introduced the agenda item. 
 
Applicant Representative Roscoe Witham presented to the podium. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed the building’s history, sharing that the circa 1928 Coe Building was 
designed by architects Crowell and Lancaster. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked if the project rendering displays a newly painted soffit – Applicant 
Representative Witham responded that if pieces of the soffit are unable to be replaced, they will be 
painted white. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed the metal moldings on the window perimeters that clamp onto existing 
metal panels. He asked if this is to remain with the newly installed faux brick panels. Applicant 
Representative Witham responded that the windows will have a J channel that will meet up to the brick. 
 
Chair King asked the Commission for questions. 
 
Commissioner Keebler asked if the faux brick is vinyl – Applicant Representative Witham responded the 
material is similar to vinyl but offers more sturdiness. Keebler asked if the faux brick is the same size as 
rest of the building’s brick – Witham confirmed. 
 
Commissioner Krupke asked to see a sample – Applicant Representative Witham provided an image. 
 
Commissioner Krupke asked about a remaining square box panel – Applicant Representative Witham 
shared it is believed to have been an alarm for the former jewelry store. HPC Consultant Pullen 
requested removal if it is no longer operational – Applicant Representative Witham confirmed he would 
like to remove it. 
 
Commissioner Keebler expressed he appreciates the approach and asked what material is under the 
current exterior. Applicant Representative Witham responded 3/4 inch plywood. 
 
Commissioner Krupke expressed support for the proposed service windows. 
 
Commissioner Sachs asked if language needed to be added surrounding the removal of the square box 
panel. HPC Consultant Pullen shared that it will be recorded in the minutes. Planning Officer Collette 
recommended including it in the decision, as Code Enforcement primarily references the decision letter.  
 
Chair King opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the procedural background was appropriately fulfilled. Seconded by 
Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that Part 2, Sections 3, 5, 6, and 8, as well as
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
August 13th, 2026 
Part 3, Sections 1, 2, and 3, are not applicable to this application. Seconded by Commissioner Krupke. 
All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 2, the 
application satisfied Historic Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic 
structure will preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. Seconded by Commissioner 
Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 2, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not 
destroy the distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. Seconded by 
Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 2, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(a) requiring that every reasonable effort 
shall be made to provide a compatible use which will require minimum alteration to the structure and its 
environment. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion 
passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 2, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features 
or examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not damaged or destroyed, 
wherever possible. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 2, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(g) requiring contemporary design for 
additions to only be approved if such design is compatible with the size, scale, material, and character of 
the neighborhood, structures, or its environment. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 2, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) requiring that, wherever possible, all 
alterations to structures shall be done in such a manner that if they were to be removed in the future, the 
essential form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. Seconded by Commissioner 
Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of 
Section IV of this document, the Project meets the requirements for a Certificate of Appropriateness and 
therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review Permit for the proposed Project, 
with the condition that the square box panel above the second window be removed if at all possible, and 
if not possible to remove, be painted in like color to its surrounding wall. Seconded by Commissioner 
Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
4. Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review – 139 Main Street – Map-Lot 
042-130 – Main Street Historic District – Applicant: Renewal by Anderson - Owner: 
Ryan York - The applicant, Renewal by Anderson, requests approval for Certificate of 
Appropriateness and Design Review at property located at 139 Main Street for the 
replacement of three windows and one entry door with in-kind materials. The property is 
located at Map-Lot 042-130 in the Main Street Historic District. Applicant: Renewal by 
Anderson. Owner: Ryan York
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
August 13th, 2026 
 
Chair King introduced the agenda item. 
 
Applicant Representative Caitlyn Arellano presented to the podium. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed the building’s history, sharing the William Lewis Heirs Building was 
constructed between 1858 and 1859. He noted the Romanesque arched masonry details on the front 
façade. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the glass area in all replacement windows and doors will match 
the original dimensions – Applicant Representative Arellano confirmed. Pullen shared that the windows 
are costume made and no fillers are planned around the perimeters.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the divided light muntin grills include interior and exterior grills 
and a dark spacer between the glass panes, and whether the new muntins with match the narrow width 
of those existing. Applicant Representative Arellano responded that the new materials will be the same 
size, configuration, and color as the current materials. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the exterior storm panels will be removed – Applicant 
Representative Arellano confirmed there is no longer need for the storm windows.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the exterior trim around the windows will be painted black – 
Applicant Representative Arellano responded the trim will not be touched or altered. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the diamond leaded windows will remain unaltered – Applicant 
Representative Arellano confirmed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler asked what materials are being used – Applicant Representative Arellano 
responded fibrex, a hybrid material designed to withstand and prevent fading. Keebler asked if the 
windows are impregnated with the black color – Arellano confirmed.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the glass would be tinted or clear – Applicant Representative 
Arellano responded clear. 
 
Commissioner Keebler asked about the double pane windows – Applicant Representative Arellano 
described they will use an insert frame that is not visible from outside. Keebler commented the project is 
as close as the applicant can accomplish to like materials and creates better sealing. 
 
Chair King opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Commissioner Coe moved that the application was deemed complete on August 13, 2026, the proposed 
project is a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review, and the applicant paid all applicable fees. 
Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.  
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-6, the application 
satisfied Historic Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic structure will 
preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. Seconded by Seconded by Commissioner 
Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that Part 2, Section 1, 5, 6, 7, and 8, and Part 
3, Sections 1, 2, and 3, are not applicable to this application. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
August 13th, 2026 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-6, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not destroy 
the distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. Seconded by 
Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-6, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(c) requiring that, while repair is preferable to 
replacement, in the event that replacement of deteriorate architectural features is necessary, the feature 
being replaced in color, design, texture and other visual qualities and, where economically and 
technically feasible, materials. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-6, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features or 
examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not damaged or destroyed, 
wherever possible. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that The Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-6, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) requiring that, wherever possible, all alterations to 
structures shall be done in such a manner that if they were to be removed in the future the essential 
form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of 
Section IV of this document, the Project meets the requirements for a Certificate of Appropriateness and 
therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review for the proposed Project. 
Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
5. Adjournment 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:33 PM.  
 
Respectfully submitted,  
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant 
Planning Division
